c74object.name: mUnit.assert
c74object.digest: Check inputs against a JavaScript expression, as a test in an mUnit suite
c74object.description: mUnit.assert is the test object of mUnit. It receives inputs on its data inlets and evaluates a JavaScript expression over them: the expression refers to the inputs as in1 to in10, and passes when it returns exactly true. The verdict is reported to mUnit.handler, which writes the results of the whole suite, and the box turns green (passed), red (failed) or yellow (skipped).
c74object.discussion: Ints, floats, symbols, lists, dicts and Jitter matrices are all passed to the expression as values, so in1 === 'foo', in1.length === 3, in1.name === 'munit' and in1.dim[0] == 64 all work. Helpers such as approx, equals, snapshot, rms and planeMean report expected and actual values when they fail. Instead of an expression, the name of a JavaScript file makes a custom assert. The object keeps as many data inlets as the highest inN the expression uses, up to 10; the first inlet is reserved for the framework. in1 is hot: a value there evaluates the expression with the latest other inputs, and a bang there evaluates again. Feed the inputs from mUnit.loadbang, not loadbang, so they are not sent before the handler is ready. Each assert is posted to the Max console as it finishes and written to the results. assert is an alias kept for old patches.

inlet.digest: Framework control; do not send test inputs here
inlet.description: Used by the mUnit framework. Values sent here are ignored with a warning.
A value here evaluates the expression with the latest values of the other inputs. A bang evaluates again with the stored values.
Stored until the next evaluation. The object keeps as many of these inlets as the expression uses (dataInlets for custom asserts).

objarg.name: expression
objarg.digest: The JavaScript expression, or the name of a custom assert script
objarg.description: Any JavaScript expression over in1 to in10; the default is in1 === 1. Quote an expression that contains commas, e.g. "approx(in1, 0.5, 0.001)", so Max keeps it as one argument, and write string literals with single quotes, since Max strips double quotes from the arguments of an object box. A name ending in .js loads a custom assert: a script on the search path that exports a function taking the inputs as an array and returning a State from libmunit (Success, Fail, Continue, Skipped), or { state, expected, actual, message, attachments }.

method.name: bang
method.digest: Evaluate again with the stored inputs
method.description: In the in1 inlet: evaluates the expression with the stored values of every input. Counts as a call.

method.name: int
method.description: In a data inlet: the input for that inlet. In in1 it also evaluates the expression.

method.name: float
method.description: In a data inlet: the input for that inlet. In in1 it also evaluates the expression.

method.name: list
method.digest: A list input, seen by the expression as an array
method.description: In a data inlet: the input for that inlet, as a JavaScript array, so in1.length, in1[0], equals(in1, [1, 2, 3]) and the measures (rms, peak, dc, maxDiff, snr) apply.

method.name: anything
method.description: In a data inlet: a symbol (or a symbol followed by values, as a list) is the input for that inlet. Compare it with single quotes: in1 === 'foo'.

method.name: dictionary
method.digest: A dict input, seen by the expression as an object
method.description: In a data inlet: the dict's contents, as a plain JavaScript object: in1.name === 'munit', equals(in1, {...}) or snapshot(in1).

method.name: jit_matrix
method.description: In a data inlet: the matrix as a value with dim, planes, type and every cell, for planeMin, planeMean, planeMax, cell and sameMatrix, or for comparison with a reference file. Char cells are 0 to 255.

attribute.name: maxCalls
attribute.digest: How many inputs the assert evaluates (default 1)
attribute.description: An expression assert fails once it has been false this many times; a custom assert passes once it reaches this many calls without failing. After the verdict, further inputs are ignored and logged.

attribute.name: every
attribute.description: Expression asserts: every call must be true, up to maxCalls, instead of any one of them. With maxCalls this checks a table of cases; it fails on the first false case and says which call it was.

attribute.name: tolerance
attribute.digest: How many failing calls are tolerated (default 0)
attribute.description: Custom and every asserts: how many Fail results are tolerated before the assert fails.

attribute.name: timeout
attribute.digest: How long the assert may take, in ms (default none)
attribute.description: The clock starts when the suite starts (when mUnit.loadbang fires) or at the first input, whichever comes first. A timeout counts as a failed call and the clock restarts until maxCalls is reached, so @timeout 2000 @maxCalls 3 allows up to 6 seconds. Values of 0 or less are rejected.

attribute.name: accumulate
attribute.digest: Sum the inputs over the calls before evaluating (default 0)
attribute.description: Expression asserts only: each input is summed (or, for symbols, concatenated) over successive calls before the expression sees it.

attribute.name: skip
attribute.description: The assert is reported as skipped without being evaluated, and its box turns yellow. Skipped asserts neither pass nor fail the suite.

attribute.name: only
attribute.digest: Skip every other assert in the suite (default 0)
attribute.description: When any assert in the suite has only, every other one is skipped without being evaluated, and its box turns yellow. An assert that finished before the only assert was loaded (an earlier patch in a sequential run) has already run; it is still reported as skipped. Set forbidOnly: true in the configuration on CI, so one can't be committed by mistake.

attribute.name: name
attribute.digest: A name for the test (default: its UUID)
attribute.description: Used in the console, the log and the results. Every assert also has a UUID, which changes on each run and appears in all logging. A snapshot uses the name for its reference file.

attribute.name: suite
attribute.digest: The suite the test belongs to (default: the parent patcher's name)
attribute.description: Groups tests in the results; each suite becomes a testsuite in JUnit output.

attribute.name: dataInlets
attribute.digest: How many data inlets a custom assert keeps (default 1)
attribute.description: Custom asserts only: a script can't say how many inputs it needs, so set this. Expression asserts count their own.

attribute.name: reference
attribute.digest: A Jitter matrix file to compare the input with
attribute.description: The name of a .jxf file in references/ next to the test patch. The matrix on in1 is compared with it instead of evaluating an expression, within maxDiff and maxFraction. A missing reference fails and says how to take it; when taking references (munit run --take-references, takeReferences: true in the configuration, or a takeReferences 1 message to mUnit.handler) the matrix is written as the reference. A failure keeps the matrix as actual.jxf and actual.png, the difference as diff.png, and links the reference.

attribute.name: maxDiff
attribute.digest: The largest difference a cell may have from the reference (default 0)
attribute.description: In the matrix's units: 0 to 255 for char. Used with reference and by sameMatrix.

attribute.name: maxFraction
attribute.digest: The largest fraction of cells that may exceed maxDiff (default 0)
attribute.description: @maxDiff 2 @maxFraction 0.001 is the perceptual rule "at most 0.1% of pixels differ by more than 2/255", which GPU output needs, since drivers differ.

entry.name: approx(actual, expected, abs = 1e-6, rel = 0)
entry.description: Numbers, lists or dicts match, numbers within max(abs, rel * abs(expected)).

entry.name: equals(actual, expected)
entry.description: Lists, dicts and symbols match exactly, dict keys in any order.

entry.name: snapshot(actual, name?)
entry.description: The value matches references/<name>.json next to the test patch; the name defaults to name. Written when taking references.

entry.name: rms(x), peak(x), dc(x), maxDiff(a, e), snr(a, reference)
entry.description: Measures over a list of numbers: root mean square, largest absolute value, mean, largest difference, and signal-to-noise ratio in dB.

entry.name: planeMin(m, plane), planeMean(m, plane), planeMax(m, plane), cell(m, x, y, plane?), sameMatrix(a, e, maxDiff, maxFraction)
entry.description: Statistics of a Jitter matrix's plane (planes from 0), one cell (or all its planes), and a comparison of two matrices with tolerances that reports the differences.
